articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI officially rolled out GPT-5, featuring significantly improved long-horizon reasoning, native image and audio generation, and a unified architecture that collapses what were previously separate models into a single end-to-end system. Benchmarks show substantial gains on PhD-level science QA and complex multi-step coding tasks, narrowing the gap to domain-specialist systems.

articles.title: Google DeepMind Unveils Gemini 2.5 Ultra with One-Million-Token Production Context
articles.summary: DeepMind released Gemini 2.5 Ultra, making its one-million-token context window generally available through Vertex AI and the Gemini API with significantly reduced latency compared to earlier long-context previews. The model demonstrates near-perfect recall across the full window, enabling enterprise use cases such as entire-codebase reasoning and full-corpus legal analysis.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude 4 with Improved Agentic Tool Use and Safety Benchmarks
articles.summary: Anthropic released Claude 4, emphasizing reliable multi-step agentic workflows where the model can autonomously chain tool calls, browse the web, and write and execute code within sandboxed environments. The release includes a new safety evaluation framework co-developed with external auditors, setting a transparency precedent for frontier model deployments.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen-3 Begins Limited Deployment in Automotive Manufacturing Lines
articles.summary: Tesla confirmed that its third-generation Optimus humanoid robot has started performing repetitive assembly and materials-handling tasks at two of its North American factories. The Gen-3 hardware features improved actuator density in the hands, enabling fine manipulation of small components like wire harnesses—a task previous generations could not reliably perform.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Toyota Research Institute Demo Learned Dexterous Manipulation on Atlas
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics, in collaboration with Toyota Research Institute, showcased the electric Atlas performing dexterous bi-manual manipulation tasks learned entirely in simulation and transferred zero-shot to hardware. The demo included assembling multi-part fixtures, representing a major milestone in sim-to-real transfer for humanoid platforms operating in unstructured environments.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 2nm GAA Chips, First Customer Silicon Ships
articles.summary: TSMC announced that its N2 process node using gate-all-around (GAA) nanosheet transistors has entered volume production at its Hsinchu Fab 20, with first customer shipments underway. The node delivers roughly 15% speed improvement and 30% power reduction over N3E, with Apple and NVIDIA among the expected early adopters for next-generation mobile and data-center processors.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Begins: First Compliance Audits Target Foundation Model Providers
articles.summary: The European Union's AI Office initiated its first formal compliance audits under the AI Act's provisions for general-purpose AI models, requesting technical documentation from several major foundation model providers. The audits focus on systemic risk assessments, compute reporting thresholds, and red-teaming documentation, marking the transition from policy to active enforcement.

articles.title: Microsoft and Quantinuum Demonstrate Reliable Logical Qubit Operations Below Error-Correction Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Quantinuum published results showing sustained logical qubit error rates below the fault-tolerance threshold across dozens of sequential operations on their latest trapped-ion system. The achievement brings practical quantum error correction closer to reality and supports Microsoft's roadmap toward a hybrid classical-quantum cloud offering integrated into Azure.
